leagues.name: Kontinental Hockey League (KHL)
notes: 22 clubs: 19 Russian, plus Dinamo Minsk (Belarus), Barys Astana (Kazakhstan) and Shanghai Dragons (China).
Title partner FONBET: the league championship is branded 'FONBET KHL Championship'; KHL.ru (2026-05-29) reported the title deal extended to 2027/28.
Russian clubs remain barred from IIHF competitions in 2026-27; the IIHF Council reaffirmed the ban on 2026-07-30.
khl.ru and several club sites return HTTP 403 to automated fetches; partner data was taken from club partner pages and a syndicated 2026-27 KHL partner widget on club sites.
No front-of-shirt (jersey) sponsor placements could be documented from reachable sources; kit entries carry sourced club partners with placement 'partner' and sponsorsComplete false.

proposedRatings.reasoning: Rosneft is majority state-owned (Wikipedia lead; primary filing not yet opened) and is the general sponsor of HC CSKA Moscow. The state is a direct party to the war in Ukraine, so the existing russian-federation-record claim carries over once ownership is verified.

Gazprom Neft is a subsidiary of state-controlled Gazprom (lead; primary document not yet opened); general partner of HC Avangard (G-Drive Arena) and club sponsor of SKA. Inherit Gazprom's severe framing via the parent once the subsidiary chain is documented.
Rostelecom is described as state-controlled (Wikipedia lead; primary ownership document not yet opened) and is a KHL league partner in 2026-27.
Russian Railways is state-owned (Wikipedia lead; primary document not yet opened); partner of HC Sochi and linked to Lokomotiv Yaroslavl.
AvtoVAZ is state-controlled via Rostec (Wikipedia lead; primary document not yet opened); KHL league partner and title sponsor of HC Lada. Indirect control, hence concern rather than serious.

SOGAZ was founded by Gazprom and is reported as sanctioned by the EU/UK (2022) and the US (2024, citing insurance for Russian military personnel) in the coverage targets research; KHL general partner. Needs a primary ownership/sanctions document before rating.

unsourced: Front-of-shirt (jersey) sponsors for all 22 KHL clubs in 2026-27: no club announced or documented a shirt-front sponsor on a page we could open. KHL jerseys typically carry only club crests and league branding, and club partner lists do not state jersey placement.

SKA Saint Petersburg ownership: 'owned by Russian state-controlled energy giant Gazprom' (infobox: Gazprom Export) per Wikipedia (lead only); corroborating primary document not opened. The archived ska.ru sponsors page (2026-03-24) lists Gazprom only as general sponsor.
KHL board chair Gennady Timchenko, also president/chair of SKA: sanctioned by the US (2014) and UK (2022) per Inside the Games (lead in targets.json; article not opened this pass).

Club ownership per Wikipedia (leads only, no primary source opened): Metallurg Magnitogorsk - Viktor Rashnikov / MMK; Ak Bars Kazan - Tatneft; HC CSKA Moscow - Rosneft (majority state-owned); HC Spartak Moscow - Investbank; Severstal Cherepovets - Alexei Mordashov; Torpedo Nizhny Novgorod - GAZ Group; Neftekhimik - NKNH (Nizhnekamskneftekhim); Admiral Vladivostok - Vladivostok sea port; Barys Astana - Kazakhstan Temir Zholy; Amur Khabarovsk - Sukhoi; Sibir Novosibirsk - Novosibirsk Oblast administration; Dinamo Minsk - BFSO Dinamo; Lokomotiv Yaroslavl - Russian Railways; HC Dynamo Moscow - VTB (site shows VTB as general sponsor, not owner); Salavat Yulaev, HC Sochi, Avtomobilist, Traktor, Lada - no owner named (Lada's club partners page lists founders samregion.ru and polyplast-un.ru as 'Учредитель').

Official club sites unreachable from this machine (curl connection failures or SPA with no server-rendered partner data): lokomotiv.ru, metallurg.ru, ak-bars.ru, neftekhimik.ru, salavat-yulaev.ru, avtomobilist.ru, admiral (hcadmiral.ru), sibir (hc-sibir.ru), barys.kz, Kunlun/Shanghai Dragons domains. Sponsor placements for these 11 clubs remain empty.
ska.ru returned HTTP 403 on live fetch and has no Wayback snapshot after 2026-03-24 with status 200; SKA partner data is from the 2026-03-24 snapshot labelled season 2025/2026.

League official partner changed between seasons: KHL.ru (2026-05-29) named SBP official partner for 2025/26; the 2026-27 club-site widget names the MIR card instead. No announcement of the switch was found.

Shanghai Dragons: rebranded from Kunlun Red Star on 2025-08-07; home listed as SKA Arena, St Petersburg; Ilya Kovalchuk president since 2026 (Wikipedia lead only). Whether it relocates to Shanghai for 2026-27 is unconfirmed.

State-control facts needing primary sources before claims can be written: Rosneft majority state ownership; Rostelecom state control; RZD state ownership; AvtoVAZ control via Rostec; Gazprom Neft as Gazprom subsidiary; SOGAZ-Gazprom founding relationship and sanctions listings; VTB state control.

FONBET is also described on hawk.ru as 'partner of the hockey clubs Avangard, Metallurg, Salavat Yulaev and Lokomotiv Yaroslavl'; individual club partnerships with Metallurg and Lokomotiv could not be confirmed on club pages.
Salavat Yulaev's own site (hcsalavat.ru) carries no partners page, only the KHL partner widget and FONBET betting links; no club sponsor documented.

KHL 2026-27 league partner set per the syndicated club-site widget ('Партнеры Фонбет Чемпионата КХЛ сезона 2026-2027'): FONBET title, SOGAZ and T-Bank general, MIR official, Rostelecom / LADA / Kinopoisk / Gislaved / Haier / S7 partners - corroborated on hawk.ru, severstalclub.ru, hcsochi.ru, hcdinamo.by, cska-hockey.ru, hcsalavat.ru, hcamur.ru.
